name: Rod of Channeling
summary: In the Wetlands, Dragonmaw spellcasters carry the Rod of Channeling. Strahad Farsan needs three for his acolytes to steady a felhunter summoning circle in Ratchet.

sections.title: Instruments of Binding
sections.body:
Warlocks need more than willpower to bind a felhunter. Strahad Farsan asks for three matched rods so his acolytes can channel magic together and steady the summoning circle as the warlock binds the beast. Dragonmaw darkcasters carry the rods for their own workings.

At Angerfang Encampment and in the surrounding Wetlands ruins, Dragonmaw Bonewarders and shadowwarders bear the rods. Combat leaves them worn and nicked, yet they still focus chaotic nether energy.

faq.q: What is the Rod of Channeling used for?
aliases: why do i need rod of channeling
faq.answer: Strahad Farsan, above Ratchet, needs the rods for his acolytes. They channel magic to steady the circle where a warlock summons and binds a hostile felhunter.

faq.q: Where can Rods of Channeling be found?
aliases: where to get rods of channeling
faq.answer: Dragonmaw spellcasters carry the rods in the Wetlands. Dragonmaw Bonewarders and Shadowwarders bear them around Angerfang Encampment.

faq.q: Why does Strahad need three rods?
faq.answer: Strahad's acolytes assist with the felhunter summoning ritual. Each needs a focus to steady the conduit while the warlock subdues the beast.

faq.q: Why are the Dragonmaw using these rods?
faq.answer: The Dragonmaw clan uses the rods in its dark shamanism and shadowcraft, remnants of the Old Horde. Its bonewarders and shadowwarders channel curses, necromancy and shadow magic in their ongoing territorial wars in the Wetlands.

angles.text: As a warlock, you gather three Rods of Channeling during the Tome of the Cabal trials. They help contain the ritual as you bind your first felhunter.
